pins.kicker: Pack swinging on the way down?
pins.title: Pack heavy close
pins.sub: Water and food go close to your back, light things outside. Clip the chest and waist straps, then pull the shoulder straps snug.

pins.kicker: Cold hands on a winter hike?
pins.title: Warm your core
pins.sub: When your core cools, your body cuts blood flow to your hands first. Gloves on before fingers get cold, a warm layer, a snack and a spare dry pair.

pins.title: Free park entry
pins.sub: Entrance fees are waived for US residents. In Yellowstone most roads are closed to cars since Nov 1, but the North Entrance road to Lamar Valley stays open, weather permitting.

pins.title: See what's inside
pins.sub: 30 printable pages: timed entry explained, 1, 2 and 3-day plans, and 18 day hikes in mi and km from nps.gov.

pins.title: Keep it warm
pins.sub: Cold weakens batteries. Charge it full the night before, carry it in an inside pocket until you need it, and always pack a backup light.

pins.title: Be seen on trail
items: An orange vest for your dog
Check dates with your state wildlife agency
pins.sub: Season dates and rules differ by state and by land, so look them up before you go.

pins.kicker: Shivering at the car after a hike?
pins.title: Dry layer first
items: Leave a dry shirt in the car
pins.sub: A wet layer pulls heat from you fast once you stop moving.

pins.title: Have a plan B
pins.sub: High roads can close for snow and ice, and Kuwohi Road closes for winter at the end of November. Check road status that morning and keep a lower trail ready.

pins.title: Carry your water
pins.sub: Free entry for US residents on Veterans Day. Bright Angel Trail water runs May to October, so in November carry all you need from the rim.

pins.kicker: Cold on your first night out?
pins.title: Fix the pad
pins.sub: The cold comes up from the ground, and a bag squashed under you can't hold heat. Pick a pad made for cold ground and sleep in dry layers and a hat.
